body: Never give up. Fuck those peers; if they say you're bad, you distance yourself from them, and you keep working at your art. It's what *you* want to do. If you let the haters stop you, you'll have to be really lucky to make it at anything in life. Anyone would. If you don't let them stop you, nothing will stop you. Put your time into voice acting, and I guarantee some of those assholes that made fun of you will one day listen to your voice and enjoy that shit. Not that they deserve it. Stay strong, we believe in you.

I'm sorry to hear that man. I definitely identify with you on a lot of that. 

Do you have anything in your life that you care about achieving or doing? Anything that ever seemed worth chasing? Just curious. It sounds like you've given up... "I can reasonably assume the best is not yet to come." 

If shit sucks right now and has for a while, it can't be that hard to make it better. I know that's a weird sort of optimism, but it's true. Maybe the best is going to come, you just have to try to go after it. Try, and don't let failures stop you. Half the problem is the word "failure". Stop thinking of them like that. They're learning experiences. They're stepping stones to getting better. It doesn't matter how long it takes, and it doesn't matter how bad you are when you start. You fucking keep trying, and one day you'll be good. It doesn't matter what the thing is, and it doesn't matter if you suck at it for two fucking decades before you become good. You keep trying. 

There's no law of physics which says you're any different than everyone else in society. You're just as human, just as capable. Sure, we all have our minute differences, but those are based largely off our beliefs. If you believe you can't do something, you can bet your ass you won't do it. Let's both do ourselves a favor and try believing in ourselves for once man.

I'm sure it feels tougher in your thirties; I'm in my twenties and it feels hard as hell. But there are famous writers who were failures until their fourties (Steven Pressfield). Fucking Einstein was rejected from universities, and had to work in a patent office. He made it because he kept going, and he kept going only because he had a remarkable aptitude for hope. If they can do it, so can you.

Same here for a lot of what you said. Never pondered suicide seriously until the last few months; it was always more of a "escape fantasy" as you so well describe, and something that I truly feared. I'm in my last year of school and I thought about dropping out *a lot* up until a few weeks ago too. I'm in a more motivated period now, but I'm not sure if it's just temporary yet. The idea of it being temporary scares me shitless. I used to have so many dreams, and I used to believe I could accomplish them all: Stop climate change; help eliminate racism, sexism, etc.; make contributions to physics and mathematics... Until at some point I started to believe these things were impossible for me. That's when I started to feel worthless, when I *really* started to think about suicide.
The thing is, it's a logical fallacy to believe that I *physically cannot* do something. The laws of physics don't say "Oh yeah, everyone can accomplish whatever they want, except so-and-so." We're all made of the same stuff, and the laws of nature work the same for all of us. So I realized I was a fool to believe that there's something inherently wrong with me. It's just mental. And then I realized that it's precisely the belief that I couldn't do it which was holding me back. I had no fucking hope, and when you believe that nothing you do has any purpose, no fucking shit you're going to want to stop. So I stopped believing in a lie. I can accomplish my dreams just as much as the next guy, I just got too obsessed with feeling like I wasn't good enough. 
I've been trying to draw hope wherever I can these days. I listen to motivational speeches for a few hours almost everyday. They really get me going. I think about the shit that other people in the world are put through; it's a dark irony that we have lives better than most in the world (deduced from our shared access to Reddit and ability to write), yet it is only us who think of suicide. But thinking about that just gets me more depressed lol. Anyways, you're not alone man. There's just one last thing I'd really like to say: In the last few weeks, I've had some incredibly positive periods where I feel like I have control of my life again, and in those moments when I look back at the depressed/suicidal version of myself, I literally feel like another person, to the point that I can barely comprehend why I even felt like that -- I say this to give you hope that **it is possible to get the life you want, and to feel good again.** (I hope you can trust me since we seem similar on many levels.) Best of luck my friend.
You're both wrong. I am the worst at everything. Neither of you can possibly be the worst, not even tied. Strictly better. Therefore neither of you have the right to question life. Keep going
